prompt: A lawn sprinkler sprays water $15$ ft in every direction across a $140^\circ$ arc. How many square feet of lawn does it water? Round to the nearest tenth.
hint: The watered patch is a sector: a slice of a circle with radius $15$ ft.

hints.text: The watered patch is a sector: a slice of a circle with radius $15$ ft.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with half a circle: a $180^\circ$ spray of radius $10$ ft covers $\frac{180}{360} \times \pi(10)^2 = 50\pi \approx 157.1$ sq ft. Same fraction-of-a-circle recipe, just with $\frac{140}{360}$ and radius $15$.
Sector area $= \frac{140}{360} \times \pi (15)^2$. Note that $15$ is the radius, since the spray reaches $15$ ft out from the sprinkler.

explanation: The spray distance $15$ ft is the radius, so the full circle would cover $\pi(15)^2 = 225\pi \approx 706.86$ sq ft.
The sprinkler only sweeps $140^\circ$ of that, a fraction of $\frac{140}{360} \approx 0.3889$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Estimate to check
steps: $140^\circ$ is a bit more than a third of a full turn.
A third of $707$ is about $236$, so an answer a little above that — $274.9$ — is believable.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: A common wrong answer is $68.7$ sq ft, from treating $15$ ft as the DIAMETER and using $r = 7.5$. The problem says the water travels $15$ ft outward from the sprinkler, and a distance measured from the center is a radius.
Also watch the other trap: $706.9$, the whole circle, forgetting to take the $\frac{140}{360}$ share. Write the fraction down first, before you ever square the radius.
